exclusion_quote: In this chapter, the details of hydrogen absorption and desorption mechanism on the CnanoHx−LiH composite is discussed on the basis of the experimental results obtained by various kinds of analyses.

I1.quote: Searched for H2 uptake measured from the gas phase gravimetrically, volumetrically or by flow. Found only TG weight loss on heating (thermal desorption; Fig. 1, Fig. 7 axis 'Desorbed Hydrogen (mass %)'); no uptake value is reported for the rehydrogenation.

I5.quote: Recently, hydrogen storage and transportation are being studied all over the world as the key technology to establish clean and renewable energy systems for a sustainable society.

notes: Book chapter (InTech, 'Advances in Diverse Industrial Applications of Nanocomposites', ch. 5) that summarizes the authors' earlier papers: every figure is attributed to a prior article (Fig. 1: Ichikawa et al., 2005, Miyaoka et al., 2009; Figs. 2, 6, 7: Miyaoka et al., 2009; Figs. 3-5: Miyaoka et al., 2008; Figs. 8-10: Miyaoka et al., 2007), and methods are deferred to earlier work ('The details of sample preparation are shown in the previous articles', p. 2, Section 2.1). Coded not_primary as a review of the group's own published work. not_primary precedes the I1-failure code no_conditions_stated in the section 4 order, so the paper is excluded on either reading. I1: the only hydrogen amounts are TG weight losses during TDMS heating to 500 C after rehydrogenation at 350 C under 3 MPa H2 ('The 1st and 2nd rehydrogenated composites can desorb 5.0 mass % of hydrogen as shown in their TG profiles', p. 4); hydrogen is held as C-H bonds and LiH. Informational: no specific surface area appears anywhere in the text or figures (searched surface, BET, m2, Langmuir), so I4 would also fail if assessed. duplicate_data would also apply on the figure attributions, but it is last in order.
